the design and validation of intrusion detection and response protocols in CPSs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we design and analyze intrusion detection protocols in a cyber physical system with the objective of maximizing the CPS lifetime in presence of malicious nodes exhibiting a wide range of attacker behaviors.
we have designed and validated intrusion detection protocols for CPSs with adaptive control that can maximize CPS lifetime in the face of malicious attacks and other sources of uncertainty.
we have developed a new model based analysis methodology for intrusion detection protocols for CPSs, which can be extended to analyze other CPS security protocols.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optimal intrusion detection and response settings depend on the attacker model, and that adaptive control for optimizing the IDS performance is essential for achieving the highest CPS reliability and lifetime in the presence and attacks.

a model-based analysis of the CPS reliability or CPS lifetime under attack is essential in the design of intrusion detection and response protocols to maximize the CPS lifetime and minimize the impact of attacks.

we provide a novel methodology for designing intrusion detection and response systems for CPSs, and we demonstrate that our designs can significantly improve CPS reliability and lifetime in the presence malicious attacks and other uncertainties.
